description.narrative: Project development objectives are to: (i) improve the financial literacy of Russian citizens (especially, among the school-ageandcollege students, and active and potential low- and middle-income users of financial services); and (ii) strengthen thefoundations for improving consumer protection in financial services.

The objectives of the Financial Education and Financial Literacy Project are to (i) improve the financial literacy of Russian citizens (especially, among the school-age and college students, and active and potential low and middle income users of financial services) and (ii) strengthen the foundations for improving consumer protection in financial services. This project has five components. Component one comprises of developing a financial literacy strategy and consumer protection monitoring and evaluation. This includes strengthening the institutional and legal framework for the implementation of financial literacy and consumer protection policies, and development of the Project monitoring and evaluation framework. Component two consists of financial literacy capacity building. This involves building institutional and human capacity for raising financial literacy in Russia at both federal and regional levels, and in the public and private sectors. Component three comprises of development and implementation of education programs and information campaigns for improving financial literacy. This includes development and implementation of educational programs, information campaigns, and the scaling up of existing financial literacy improvement initiatives. Component four consists of the strengthening of consumer protection in financial services by strengthening capacity for financial consumer protection in the Consumer Protection Service, industry professional associations, and civil society. Component five is project management which includes implementation, monitoring, and evaluation as set forth by the rules and procedures of the IBRD and Russian laws and regulations.

comment.narrative:
<p>The Funds of Good Ideas is a demand driven instrument thus through open calls it finances a number of initiatives from the open call (games, posters, digital apps, training for prisoners etc.). Thus, the innovation and qualitative aspects of the initiates are the critical part of this, not the absolute number of initiates funded. The indicator  demonstrated a very positive trend during the course of the project. In fact, the current end target of 124 initiatives is a revised target after additional financing from the Borrower, the original target was much lower. But given that all initiatives supported through the FoGI demonstrated a lot of value for improvement of financial literacy level in all age groups it was decided to go beyond the original scopeand implement additional rounds of FoGI. The VII Fund of Good Ideas in February 2020, 54 initiatives were selected as winners were specifically focused on offline activities in the regions. Unfortunately, due to the COVID-19 pandemic, they were not feasible to implement. The MoF took the decision in August 2020 to suspend the agreements to undertake those subprojects given that the Project was due to come to a close imminently.</p>

comment.narrative: <p>Targets met and exceeded. Both sub-indicators were measured through five rounds of the Financial Literacy Survey: in 2013 (baseline for 2 pilot regions), 2015 (follow-up for the 2 pilot regions and a baseline for 7 new regions), then annually in 2018, 2019, and 2020. The associated end-of-project targets for both sub-indicators (for 2 pilot regions and 7 other regions) were already exceeded in 2018 (reaching 37.9% for the 2 pilot regions and 33.1% for the 7 other regions). The positive trend continued and by project closure the associated end-of-project target for sub-indicator 2.1.2. was exceeded by 3.3 percentage points. Sub-indicator 2.1.1. surpassed the end-of-project target again in 2019 (37.1%) and, despite a slight decline in 2020 (36.7%), the target for this sub-indicator is judged to have been met and exceeded on the basis of results in 2018 and 2019.</p>
